content.study:
Abuse of process concerns the improper use of regularly issued legal process for a purpose other than the purpose for which the process was designed. It is distinct from malicious prosecution, which focuses on the wrongful initiation of proceedings and traditionally requires proof of absence of reasonable and probable cause, malice and favourable termination.

The gravamen of abuse of process is misuse or perversion of process for an improper collateral purpose. Courts distinguish an improper use of an otherwise valid process from the mere fact that a party lost or brought an unsuccessful proceeding.

This topic is included as a dedicated Torts coverage unit so students can distinguish the doctrine from neighbouring causes of action and apply it to factual problems.

sections.heading: Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: The gravamen of abuse of process is misuse or perversion of process for an improper collateral purpose. Courts distinguish an improper use of an otherwise valid process from the mere fact that a party lost or brought an unsuccessful proceeding.

sections.heading: Essential Elements
sections.body: 1. A legal process has been properly issued or obtained. 2. The defendant uses or manipulates that process for a purpose outside its lawful procedural object. 3. The improper purpose is the operative reason for the misuse. 4. The claimant establishes legally cognisable injury or damage where damages are sought. 5. The claim is distinguished from malicious prosecution and from an ordinary unsuccessful civil proceeding.
